Rashi on Pesachim 30b:10:1.hebrew: בית חרוסת - כלי שנותנין בו חומץ וכל דבר שיש לו קיהוי, ורגילין ליתן בו קמח, ועשוי לטבל בו בשר כל ימות השנה, והקמח מתחמץ מחמת הקיהוי. ולשון חרוסת — קיהוי, אייגירו"ש בלע"ז:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:10:1.english: A charoset container - A vessel in which one places vinegar and anything that has tartness, and they are accustomed to put flour into it, and it is used to dip meat into throughout the year, and the flour becomes leavened on account of the tartness. And the term charoset [means] tartness — aigros in Old French.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:10:2.hebrew: בית שאור - כלי שהאשה שורה ומנחת בו את השאור, ונותנתו בעיסה, ופעמים שהוא שוהה שם בלילה:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:10:2.english: A leaven container - A vessel in which a woman soaks and leaves the leaven, and puts it into the dough, and at times it remains there overnight.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:12:1.hebrew: נכרי שהלוה את ישראל - מעות על חמצו קודם הפסח, ועבר עליו הפסח, מותר בהנאה. ולקמיה בגמרא מוקי לה כשהרהינו אצלו בביתו, ושוהה אצל הנכרי כל ימות הפסח; דכיון דמטא זמניה ולא פרעיה, ומחוסר גוביינא נמי לא הוה — שהרי אצלו נתון — איגלאי מילתא למפרע, דמשעה שהרהינו אצלו הוה דידיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:12:1.english: A gentile who lent to an Israelite - [He lent him] money against his chametz before Passover, and Passover passed over it, [the chametz] is permitted for benefit. And later in the Gemara, [the Gemara] establishes this [mishnah as referring to a case] where he pledged it with him in his house, and it remained with the gentile throughout all the days of Passover. For since its due date arrived and he did not repay him, and it was also not lacking collection — for it was already placed in his possession — it is revealed retroactively that from the moment he pledged it with him, it was his.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:12:2.hebrew: ישראל שהלוה את הנכרי כו' - נמי, כיון דהרהינו אצלו, ומטא זמניה ולא פרעי' — מההיא שעתא דאוזפיה, קם ליה ברשותיה:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:12:2.english: A Jew who lent [money] to a gentile, etc. - Here too, since [the gentile] deposited it as a pledge with him, and its due date arrived and he did not repay him — from the time that he lent to him, it stood in his possession.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:1.hebrew: בעל חוב - המלוה את חבירו ושיעבד לו נכסיו, שאם לא אפרע לך עד יום פלוני, גבה מנכסי, והגיע זמן ולא פרע:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:1.english: A creditor - [This refers to] one who lends [money] to another, and [the borrower] encumbered his property to him, [stipulating:] "If I do not repay you by such-and-such a day, collect from my property," and the due date arrived and he did not repay.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:2.hebrew: אביי אמר למפרע הוא גובה - גבייתו שגבה עכשיו, איגלאי מילתא דמשעה שהלווהו עמדו נכסיו הללו בחזקתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:2.english: Abaye said: He retroactively collects - [Through] his collection that he collected now, it is revealed that from the time he lent him, these properties of his [the debtor's] stood in his [the creditor's] possession.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:3.hebrew: ורבא אמר - אינן בחזקתו אלא מיכן ולהבא, ולקמיה מפרש למאי נפקא מינה:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:3.english: And Rava said - [The properties] are in his possession only from this point forward; and further on, [the Gemara] explains what the practical difference [is].

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:4.english: Anywhere that the debtor consecrated - [He consecrated] his property within the term [of the loan].

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:5.english: Or the debtor sold - He sold them to others:

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:6.hebrew: כולי עלמא לא פליגי - אפילו לרבא, דאמר עד עכשיו היו ברשות לוה, מודה הוא דאין מכירתו לאחרים מכירה, ואין הקדישו הקדש; שהרי ממושכנין הן למלוה, ואף על גב שהן שלו — אינן ברשותו. ורחמנא אמר (ויקרא כ״ז:י״ד): ״ואיש כי יקדיש את ביתו קדש״ — מה ביתו ברשותו, אף כל ברשותו:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:6.english: Everyone agrees - Even according to Rava, who said that until now they were in the debtor's domain, he concedes that his sale to others is not a [valid] sale, and his consecration is not [valid] consecration, for they are mortgaged to the creditor; and even though they belong to him, they are not in his domain. And the Merciful One stated (Leviticus 27:14): "And if a man sanctifies his house to be holy" — just as his house is in his domain, so too anything [consecrated must be] in his domain.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:13:7.english: That the creditor comes and seizes - From the purchasers without payment.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:2:1.hebrew: מאחר דאיתותב רבא בר אהילאי - ושמעינן דהיסק מועיל לכלי חרס, קדירות בפסח אמאי ישברו? יסיקם ויתלבנו:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:2:1.english: Since Rava bar Ahilai was refuted - and we learn [from this] that heating is effective for earthenware vessels, why should pots on Passover be broken? Let him heat them and they will become white-hot.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:2:2.hebrew: א"ל - רב מוקים ליה לההוא דקתני "עד שיוסק", דמשמע הא הוסק שרי — בתנור של מתכת. אבל של חרס, התורה העידה עליו שאינו יוצא מידי דופיו לעולם:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:2:2.english: [Rav Ashi] said to him - Rav establishes that which was taught, “until it is kindled” — which implies: behold, [if] it was kindled, it is permitted — as [referring to] a metal oven. But [for a vessel] of earthenware, the Torah testified concerning it that it never rids itself of its blemish.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:3:1.hebrew: חייס עלייהו - ואי שרית ליה על ידי היסק פנים, מורה היתירא וסמיך אהיסק בחוץ:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:3:1.english: He spares them - And if you were to permit him [to kasher them] by means of heating from the inside, he would rationalize permission for himself and rely on heating from the outside.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:4:1.hebrew: בוכיא - כלי שהוא מרעפים, שקורין טיילי"ש, ואופין ומטגנין בו ככר:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:4:1.english: [A] bukhya - A vessel that is [made] of tiles, which they call tuiles [tiles], and in which they bake and fry a loaf [of bread].

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:5:1.english: For me, they make new [ones] - For my needs, they make new knives.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:5:2.english: For Master it is possible - For you are wealthy.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:5:3.english: Their handles in mud - To protect them so that the fire does not burn them.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:5:4.hebrew: והלכתא - לא צריך לאותבינהו בנורא, אלא פרזלייהו — כי קתייהו — נמי סגי להו בהגעל' ברותחין:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:5:4.english: And the halakha [is] - It is not necessary to place them in fire; rather, for their iron [blades] — like their handles — purging in boiling water is also sufficient for them.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:6:1.english: A wooden ladle - [The utensil] with which one stirs the pot.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:6:2.hebrew: כבולעו כך פולטו - כבולעו מתוך כלי ראשון, כך פולטו בכלי ראשון:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:6:2.english: As it absorbs, so it emits - Just as it absorbs from within a primary vessel, so it emits in a primary vessel.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:1.hebrew: קונייא - פלומי"ר בלע"ז, ושל חרס הוא וטוח באבר:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:1.english: Glazed [konya] - Plomier in Old French; and it is [made] of earthenware and coated with lead.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:2.hebrew: ירוקי - עשויין מקרקע שחופרים ממנה צריף — אלו"ם בלע"ז — והוא עז, ובולע לעולם:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:2.english: Green [vessels] - [They are] made from earth from which alum [tzarif] is dug — alun in the vernacular — and it is potent, and absorbs permanently.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:3.hebrew: ה"ג ירוקי לא תיבעי לך דודאי אסירי דמצרפי ובלעי - דמצרפי — צריף:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:3.english: This is the correct reading: “Green [vessels], the dilemma need not be raised, for they are certainly forbidden, as they contain alum and absorb” - Dematzrifei — [meaning that they contain] alum [tzrif].

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:7:5.english: Let the dilemma be raised with regard to [those] that are smooth - That they are smooth.

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:8:1.hebrew: דמידייתי - פולטין המשקין מדופנן החיצון, ובלע"ז טרשטדט"ש. וכיון דמידייתי — ודאי בלעי; והואיל ובלעי — שוב אינן פולטין, שהתורה העידה על כלי חרס שכיון שבלע אינו יוצא מידי דופיו לעולם, שהרי בכלי עץ ומתכות כתב לך: "ישטף", "תעבירו באש", "ומורק ושוטף", אבל בכלי חרס — "ישבר":
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:8:1.english: That they seep - They discharge liquids from their outer wall; and in Old French, tresgotés [sweating through]. And since they seep, they certainly absorb; and since they absorb, they no longer discharge [what was absorbed], for the Torah testified regarding an earthenware vessel that once it has absorbed, it never leaves its tainted status forever. For regarding wooden and metal vessels, [the Torah] wrote to you: “it shall be rinsed,” “you shall pass through fire,” [and] “it shall be scoured and rinsed”; but regarding an earthenware vessel: “it shall be broken.”

Rashi on Pesachim 30b:9:1.hebrew: חמץ - תשמישו ע"י חמין כל השנה, אבל יין נסך לא נשתמש בו אלא צונן:
Rashi on Pesachim 30b:9:1.english: Chametz - Its use is with hot [food] throughout the year, but [with regard to] libation wine, it was used only cold.

Tosafot on Pesachim 30b:5:1.hebrew: והלכתא אידי ואידי ברותחין - תימה, דתניא בתוספתא דע"ז: "הסכין והשפוד והאסכלא מלבנן באור", ובפרק קמא דחולין (דף ח: ושם) אמר: "כגון שליבנה באור", אלמא צריך ליבון? ותירץ ר"ת, דאמר בירושלמי דמיירי בסכינים ארוכים שצולין בהם בשר, דומיא דשפוד; וכן ההוא דחולין. ועוד יש לחלק בין התירא בלע ובין איסורא בלע, כדמחלק רב אשי בשילהי מסכת ע"ז. והא דמצריך להו רב אשי הכא ליבון — מחמיר על עצמו היה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 30b:5:1.english: "And the halakha is that both this and that [are purged] in boiling water" - This is astonishing, for it is taught in the Tosefta of Avodah Zarah: "A knife, a spit, and a grill — one purges them with fire," and in the first chapter of Chullin (8b and there) [the Gemara] says: "For example, where he purged it with fire," which implies that it requires libbun? And Rabbeinu Tam answered that [the Talmud] says in the Yerushalmi that [those sources] are dealing with long knives with which they roast meat, similar to a spit; and so too is that [case] in Chullin. And furthermore, one can distinguish between [a utensil that] absorbed permitted [matter] and [one that] absorbed forbidden [matter], as Rav Ashi distinguishes at the end of tractate Avodah Zarah. And that which Rav Ashi here required libbun for them — he was being stringent with himself.

Tosafot on Pesachim 30b:8:1.hebrew: התורה העידה על כלי חרס שאינו יוצא מידי דופיו לעולם דכתיב ביה ישבר - וא"ת: תיפוק ליה דחזינן להו דמידייתי, והיינו אחר הגעלה — דאי לפני הגעלה, שאר כלים נמי מידייתי? וי"ל: דלעולם מיירי קודם הגעלה, וכמו שפ"ה בע"ז (דף לד.) דמידייתי בחוץ, וכיון דמידייתי מבחוץ — בלעי טפי. וא"ת: והלא יוצא מידי דופיו ע"י כבשונות, דבזבחים בפ' דם חטאת (זבחים דף צו. ושם) פריך: וליהדרינהו לכבשונות, ואמאי קדירות במקדש ישברו? ומשני: לפי שאין כבשונות בירושלים, הא יש כבשונות — שרו בחזרה לכבשונות! וכן לעיל אמר (אבל) קדירה לא, דלמא חייס עלה; הא לאו הכי — שרי קדירות בהיסק מבפנים, וכן אמר: אי מליא גומרי שפיר דמי! ואור"ת: דזה לא חשיב יוצא מידי דופיו, דכיון שהסיקו נעשה ככלי חדש, שכן דרך כלי חרס כשעושין אותו נותנו אותו בכבשן להסיקו. וא"ת: והיכי מייתי ראיה מדכתיב ישבר? דילמא גזירת הכתוב הוא, דאפי' תלאו באויר התנור — בעי התם רבא בר חמא: אי קפיד רחמנא אבישול בלא בלוע או לא? וי"ל: דלכלי נחושת מועיל שטיפה ומריקה אפילו בבישול ובלוע, א"כ מה שהקפיד בכלי חרס אבישול בלא בלוע — היינו לפי שעשאו כבישול וכבלוע. ולר"ת יש להקשות: תנור שנטמא, אמאי חולקין לשלשה? כיון דחשיב כאחד, ליעבד ליה היסק ותו לא! ונראה לרשב"א: דמיירי בקדרה שאין דרכה להסיק, כשמחזירין אותה לכבשונות — אז פנים חדשות באו לכאן; אבל תנור, כל שעה ושעה מסיקו מבפנים, ולאו כפנים חדשות דמי, וצריך שבירה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 30b:8:1.english: "The Torah testified about an earthenware vessel that it will never leave its defective status," as it is written regarding it: "It shall be broken" - And if you say: Let [the Gemara] derive it from [the fact] that we see that they sweat — and this must be after scalding, for if [it were] before scalding, other vessels also sweat! And one can say: In fact, it is dealing with [a case] before scalding, and as the commentary [of Rashi] explained in Avodah Zarah (34a), they sweat on the outside; and since they sweat on the outside, they absorb more. And if you say: But does it not leave its defective status by means of kilns? For in Zevachim, in the chapter [entitled] Dam Chatat (Zevachim 96a and there), [the Gemara] asks: "And let them return them to the kilns, and why should [earthenware] pots in the Temple be broken?", and answers: "Because there are no kilns in Jerusalem" — which implies that if there were kilns, they would be permitted by returning [them] to the kilns! And similarly above, [the Gemara] said (however): "[Firing] a pot [from within is] not [permitted], lest he have pity on it [and not heat it sufficiently for fear of cracking it]" — which implies that were it not for this, pots would be permitted by heating [them] from within; and similarly, [the Gemara] said: "If it is filled with burning coals, it is well [permitted]!" And Rabbeinu Tam says: This is not considered "leaving its defective status," because once he has fired it, it becomes like a new vessel, for such is the manner of an earthenware vessel: when they make it, they place it into a kiln to fire it. And if you say: And how does [the Gemara] bring proof from that which is written: "It shall be broken"? Perhaps it is a scriptural decree, for even if one suspended it in the airspace of the oven, Rava bar Chama asked there: Does the Merciful One insist on cooking without absorption, or not? And one can say: For a copper vessel, scouring and rinsing are effective even for cooking and absorption; if so, that which [the Torah] was stringent regarding an earthenware vessel for cooking without absorption is because [the Torah] treated it like cooking and absorption. And according to Rabbeinu Tam, one may raise an objection: An oven that became ritually impure, why must they divide it into three [parts]? Since [the fired vessel] is considered like [a new vessel], let him perform a firing for it and nothing more! And it appears to the Rashba that [Rabbeinu Tam] is dealing with a pot, which is not normally fired [from within after manufacture]; when they return it to the kilns, a "new face has arrived here" [it is considered a new vessel]. But an oven is fired from within all the time, and it is not considered like a "new face," and [therefore] it requires breaking.
